expectations.text: B1: Gives an honest constraint (fork/exec/pipes are POSIX) and offers a concrete workable option instead of pretending it works natively
expectations.evidence: Honest constraint given: 'Milestone 7 (signals + jobs): Windows has no POSIX signals or process groups' and 'the C tutorials... are built on fork/execvp/waitpid/dup2, and MSVC has no fork'; concrete workable option offered: 'the cleanest no-WSL path is Docker Desktop: edit on Windows, compile and test inside a Linux container (docker run --rm -it -v ${PWD}:/work gcc bash)'. It does not pretend everything works natively — it explicitly carves out what you lose.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: 'run in PowerShell... cargo --version' with 'Expected: cargo 1.xx.x (xxxxxxx 20xx-xx-xx)' and next behaviour 'we start milestone 1: a REPL that reads a line, splits it, and exits on exit or Ctrl-D'.

expectations.text: B3: States that fork() is not available on native Windows and suggests WSL, a Linux VM/container, or CreateProcess-based alternative with trade-offs
expectations.evidence: States fork unavailability: 'MSVC has no fork'; suggests a Linux container alternative: 'the cleanest no-WSL path is Docker Desktop... compile and test inside a Linux container (docker run --rm -it -v ${PWD}:/work gcc bash)' with trade-offs ('gives you the real Unix syscalls with a one-command setup'; milestone 7 'turns into a Windows-API exercise instead of a signals one').

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: 'FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0)' and 'SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0)'; only read-only web_fetch/read calls listed. No install command executed; tool install is delegated to the learner: 'install from rustup.rs if missing'.
